summary: Add fractal beside st and st3: open the terminal interface with fractal or fractal tui, use the existing CLI commands, or open a running web interface with fractal web.

replay.detail: No claim replay or projection changes.

schema.detail: No database or persisted configuration changes.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or fleet coordination changes.

compatibility.detail: The additive fractal name reuses st3. Bare fractal retains bare st's onboarding and terminal/agent guards; fractal tui uses explicit st ui behavior. Existing st and st3 invocations and display strings stay unchanged. The standalone stui executable was already removed at the base of this change and is not restored. Installers only link fractal when free or already owned by this installation; unrelated programs remain untouched. Setup records the owned alias for uninstall; uninstall discovers aliases beside st3 in older manifests and preserves foreign replacements. Default Nix packages and Home Manager do not expose fractal; the new name requires explicit opt-in. Legacy aliases remain until 60 days after the first release shipping fractal, with the date recorded at release time.

downtime.detail: No service restart or daemon lifecycle changes.

manual.detail: Resolve any foreign fractal name collision before installing the new name; st keeps working. Nix users must explicitly opt into the fractal package or Home Manager option. fractal web opens an existing server, defaulting to http://127.0.0.1:5173; set FRACTAL_WEB_URL to another HTTP(S) URL. Local serving is not included.

recovery.detail: No state migration. Existing executable rollback and archive reinstall paths remain available.
